problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062541/assets/0185149b5af7fc3c8d7b69be6bef4aa6364d3a8f27a3c9730dfdedeca72926f9.png)

Evaluate the triple integral 
${∭}_{R}5{x}^{2}\,dV$
over the region $R,$ shown above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the top one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062541/assets/f8704aa6c4823f6028caf14e5eef44a5a739d45476911930ae69daafc2ed05f7.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type I region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,0\le z\le 3-\frac{4x}{5}}
$$

where

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,\,0\le y\le 2}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062541/assets/31f2ff96afa1248427c1a6dd5074c47190c70983d7c0d5dfdd3def8bd883aef8.png)

Hence, we can express the region $R$ as

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 3-\frac{4x}{5}}
$$

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}5{x}^{2}\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3-4x/5}5{x}^{2}\,dz\,dy\,dx.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $x$ and $y$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3-4x/5}5{x}^{2}\,dz\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{3-4x/5}5{x}^{2}\,dz]dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}[5{x}^{2}z]_{z=0}^{z=3-4x/5}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}5{x}^{2}(3-\frac{4x}{5})\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}(15{x}^{2}-4{x}^{3})\,dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}(15{x}^{2}-4{x}^{3})\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(15{x}^{2}-4{x}^{3})[{\int }_{0}^{2}\,dy]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(15{x}^{2}-4{x}^{3})[y]_{y=0}^{y=2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}2(15{x}^{2}-4{x}^{3})\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}2(15{x}^{2}-4{x}^{3})\,dx & =2[5{x}^{3}-{x}^{4}]_{x=0}^{x=3} \\  & =2(135-81)-0 \\  & =108.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Notice that our solid can be written as the type I region

R={(x,y,z):(x,y)∈D,0≤z≤3−4x5}

where

D={(x,y):0≤x≤3,0≤y≤2}

is the projection of R onto the xy-plane, shown below.

Hence, we can express the region R as

R={(x,y,z):0≤x≤3,0≤y≤2,0≤z≤3−4x5}

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

∭R5x2dV=∫03∫02∫03−4x/55x2dzdydx.

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to z, treating x and y as constants:

∫03∫02∫03−4x/55x2dzdydx=∫03∫02[∫03−4x/55x2dz]dydx=∫03∫02[5x2z]z=0z=3−4x/5dydx=∫03∫025x2(3−4x5)dydx=∫03∫02(15x2−4x3)dydx

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to y, treating x as a constant:

∫03∫02(15x2−4x3)dydx=∫03(15x2−4x3)[∫02dy]dx=∫03(15x2−4x3)[y]y=0y=2dx=∫032(15x2−4x3)dx

Finally, we integrate with respect to x:

∫032(15x2−4x3)dx=2[5x3−x4]x=0x=3=2(135−81)−0=108.
